name: Hip flexion
pattern: Thigh lifts forward and up against resistance, standing or lying: the knee drive of sprinting and stair climbing.
setup: Stand tall side-on to a support, cable or band strap on the working ankle.
Standing knee soft, weight over the middle of that foot.
Brace your trunk so it will not lean back.

steps.text: Working leg slightly behind you, toes on the floor.
Drive the knee up and forward until the thigh is about level.
Hold a moment, trunk tall, toes up.
Lower the leg slowly back behind you.

cues.cue: Stay tall; do not lean back to lift the leg.
cues.why: Leaning back and tucking the pelvis lets the trunk fake the hip range.
The iliopsoas works hardest when the thigh is lifted high.
The standing side hip holds the pelvis level for every single-leg drive.
Hip flexor training has improved sprint and shuttle times; a fast drive matches running.

breathing: Breathe out as the knee drives up, in as it lowers.

tempo.note: Drive up in 1 second or less, hold 1, lower in 2.

mistakes.name: Leaning back
mistakes.looks: The trunk tips back and the lower back rounds as the leg rises.
mistakes.fix: Brace, chest slightly forward, use less load.
mistakes.why: The spine and pelvis are making the range, not the hip flexors.

mistakes.name: Swinging the leg
mistakes.looks: The leg is kicked up and drops back with no control.
mistakes.fix: Pause at the top and take 2 seconds to lower.
mistakes.why: Momentum does the lift; the muscle only works briefly.

mistakes.name: Standing hip drops
mistakes.looks: The standing-side hip sinks or the standing knee bends a lot.
mistakes.fix: Stand tall on that leg, squeeze its glute.
mistakes.why: The side hip muscles of the standing leg are not holding the pelvis.

safety: Front-of-hip pinching: lift only to the pain-free height.
Lower-back pain: avoid the lying straight-leg version; keep the knee bent.

variants.change: Band anchored low behind you; same keyframes.
Straight-leg lift to about 45°: harder lever.
Lying on your back, pull the knee to the chest against a cable at the foot.
Fast knee drives, often alternating or after a step-up or push-up.

subtypes.name: Lying hip flexion
subtypes.change: On your back, cable at the foot; pull the knee toward the chest, other leg straight.

subtypes.name: Knee drive
subtypes.change: Explosive knee drive with the opposite arm swinging forward, like a sprint start.

motion.basis: Right leg working, left leg standing. Hip flexor role from andersson1997; joint angles estimated for a bent-knee cable hip flexion to thigh level. No kinematic study of the cable version found.

sources.cite: Andersson EA, Nilsson J, Ma Z, Thorstensson A. Abdominal and hip flexor muscle activation during various training exercises. Eur J Appl Physiol. 1997;75(2):115-123.
Deane RS, Chow JW, Tillman MD, Fournier KA. Effects of hip flexor training on sprint, shuttle run, and vertical jump performance. J Strength Cond Res. 2005;19(3):615-621.
Haff GG, Triplett NT (eds). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, 4th ed. NSCA / Human Kinetics, 2016. Exercise technique chapters.
